clue.text: A couple of seconds to break into ground may be the mission

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it, so these letters go within the other word

parts.note: to embay is to land-lock or trap a ship in a bay, so a vessel embayed is effectively grounded
two instances of S, the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Two seconds' work to break into the ground could be the whole task at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like soil but is a verb: to embay, a Chambers word, is to shut a ship in a bay so it cannot get out.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is a diplomatic mission sent abroad, and the word is a straight synonym in that sense.

clue.text: Hard to screen dancing bear getting worse

indicators.note: screening something hides it behind or around, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: exacting means hard, demanding

indicators.note: a dancing animal moves about, so its letters are shuffled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: It is hard to hide a dancing bear, and the situation keeps deteriorating.
explanation.definitionFit: Exacerbating is making a bad situation worse; as an intransitive participle it means worsening, getting worse.

clue.text: Softens a salmon in steam? Not normally

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it
not normally means in an unusual way, so these letters are arranged abnormally

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written
lax is an old word for salmon, related to Scandinavian laks and gravlax

explanation.surface: Cooking a salmon in steam makes it tender, though that is not the usual method.
explanation.walkthrough: 'salmon' is not the fish being cooked but an old word for it, lax, still seen in gravlax.
explanation.definitionFit: To malaxate is to knead or make soft, so malaxates means softens, both third-person verbs.

clue.text: Dark-haired fellow in punt tackling course

indicators.note: tackling something means taking hold of it, so the outer word grips the inner one

parts.note: a punt is a gamble, a bet
a course, as of a river or events, is a run

explanation.surface: A dark-haired man in a punt is negotiating a river course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punt' suggests the flat-bottomed boat, but here it is the British sense of a wager.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunet is the masculine form of brunette, a man or boy with dark brown hair.

clue.text: Bring up cries about dropping English

indicators.note: turned about means facing the other way, so the word is read right to left
dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: to cry is to weep
E is the abbreviation for English; one is taken out

explanation.surface: Someone raises complaints about English being abandoned as a subject.
explanation.walkthrough: One E comes out of WEEPS, then what is left is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring up is to vomit, and spew is a blunt synonym of that verb.

clue.text: Hairy problem for detached American footballers

parts.note: split means separated, detached
ends are players on the end of the line in American football

explanation.surface: A tricky issue for some American football players who have been cut adrift.
explanation.walkthrough: A split end is in fact an American football position, a wide receiver; 'Hairy problem' sounds like slang for a difficult situation but is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Split ends are hairs whose tips have frayed into two strands, a problem that is literally hairy.

clue.text: Name of absolute Conservative in post

indicators.note: placing things in something puts them inside the surrounding word

parts.note: a post is a position of employment
A is a standard abbreviation for absolute (as in absolute temperature)
C is the usual abbreviation for Conservative

explanation.surface: Someone asks the name of a thoroughly Tory figure holding some office.
explanation.walkthrough: A and C together sit inside JOB: J-AC-OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacob is a male forename, the biblical patriarch's, so it is an example of a name.

clue.text: Extreme cold in Scottish mountain of no little breadth

definitions.note: 'in Scottish' marks the word as Scots

indicators.note: of no something means without any of it, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a jebel is a hill or mountain in Arab countries
B is the short form of breadth; this letter goes

explanation.surface: Bitter cold on a narrow Scottish peak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little breadth' sounds like a narrow summit, but 'little' marks the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeel is a Scots word for intense cold or to congeal with cold, so it names extreme cold in Scotland.

clue.text: Bearded and muscular brother coming unstuck

indicators.note: something coming unstuck falls off, so those letters are detached from the word

parts.note: brawny means strong and muscular
BR is the abbreviation for brother; it is removed

explanation.surface: A bearded, beefy brother has a mishap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bearded' seems to describe a man, but in botany a beard is the bristle on grain.
explanation.definitionFit: Awny means having awns, the bristly hairs on ears of barley or wheat, which botanists call a beard.

clue.text: Head of finance leaving, Tom's opening unappetising drink

indicators.note: a letter leaving a word departs from it, so it is no longer there

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, so his opening is a cat flap in a door

indicators.note: 'Head of' keeps only the first letter of 'finance'

parts.note: the opening letter of finance; it is removed

explanation.surface: The finance chief quits, and Tom opens with a nasty drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tom' looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: Catlap is a contemptuous word for a weak or wishy-washy drink such as thin tea, fit only for a cat to lap.

clue.text: Male bass soon improvised "I kiss your hands"

indicators.note: improvised means made up on the spot, so these letters are put together in a new order

parts.note: the three words taken together as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A male bass singer will soon be ad-libbing a courtly greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: Beso las manos is a Spanish phrase of polite greeting, literally meaning I kiss the hands, used in English as a courteous salutation.

clue.text: Strong snuff approved in enclosure at Ayr

indicators.note: something held in an enclosure is surrounded by it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ree is a Scots word for an enclosure such as a sheepfold; Ayr, a Scottish town, flags the Scots
APP is an abbreviation for approved

explanation.surface: A potent snuff gets the nod in a paddock at the Scottish racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ayr is a town in south-west Scotland, used here to mark a Scots word for a sheepfold.
explanation.definitionFit: Rappee is a coarse, strongly flavoured kind of snuff made from dark tobacco leaves.

clue.text: Pottery show reported

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the word matters, not its spelling

parts.note: to wear clothes or a smile is to show it off

explanation.surface: A pottery exhibition gets a write-up in the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Ware means manufactured goods of a kind, especially ceramics, as in earthenware or Delft ware.

clue.text: Pot due to be manufactured internally without limit

indicators.note: internally means on the inside, so the reworked letters sit within the other word

parts.note: all, the whole lot, has no limit set on it

indicators.note: manufactured means made up or fabricated, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A pot is scheduled to be made in-house, with no ceiling on output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without limit' reads as describing production, but it supplies the outer word: everything, with no limit set.
explanation.definitionFit: An aludel is a pear-shaped earthenware pot once used by alchemists for sublimation, so it is a kind of pot.

clue.text: Trainers right away producing songs from Jamaica

indicators.note: something sent away is no longer there, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: mentors are people who train or coach others
R is the usual abbreviation for right; this letter is taken out

explanation.surface: Coaches, with the correct one gone, end up producing Jamaican music.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R out of MENTORS to leave MENTOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mento is a Jamaican folk-music style that preceded ska, and mentos are songs in that style.

clue.text: Smart girl in non-league match, relieving pressure

indicators.note: relieving someone of something takes it from them, so that letter is removed

parts.note: a cup tie is a knockout cup match, as opposed to a league fixture
P is the abbreviation for pressure; it is taken out

explanation.surface: A sharp young woman appears at a cup game and takes the pressure off.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football a cup tie is a knockout match, outside the league programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutie is an attractive, appealing girl; 'smart' here means smartly turned out, attractive.

clue.text: Badly cracked, in fact set to be repaired

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together differently, so these letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
the letters of these two words, joined to the small word before them

explanation.surface: Seriously split, and indeed fixed for mending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fact' reads as a phrase meaning indeed, but all three small words are just letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatiscent is a rare word meaning gaping with chinks or cracks, so it describes something badly cracked.

clue.text: Mineral oil credit tight, small amount shared externally

indicators.note: shared externally means split around the outside, so the small amount is divided to surround the rest

parts.note: a mite is a tiny quantity

indicators.note: tight is slang for drunk, and a drunk staggers, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged
CR is the abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: Mineral oil is in a credit squeeze, with only a little to go round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tight' reads as credit being scarce, but it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Microlite is a pale-yellow to brown mineral, an oxide of tantalum found in pegmatites.

clue.text: Go out in river boat lacking power

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, a crossword regular

indicators.note: lacking something means being without it, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: a punt is a flat-bottomed boat poled along a river
P is the abbreviation for power; it is removed

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a river in a boat that has no engine.
explanation.walkthrough: EXE plus PUNT without its P gives EXEUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeunt is the Latin stage direction meaning 'they leave the stage', so it means go out.

clue.text: Attack revelry, the origin of which gets forgotten

indicators.text: the origin of which gets forgotten
indicators.note: the origin is a word's beginning, and forgetting it means that opening letter is left off

parts.note: wassail is festive drinking and merrymaking

explanation.surface: Someone attacks merrymaking, though nobody now remembers how it started.
explanation.walkthrough: WASSAIL without its first letter W leaves ASSAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail is to set upon violently or with criticism, a direct synonym of the verb attack.

clue.text: Start a task for Hindu worshipper

indicators.note: to start is to jump or twitch with surprise, so the letters are jolted out of place

parts.note: the two words as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An instruction to begin a job for a devout Hindu.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' reads as begin; here it is the startled jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sakta is a Hindu who worships Sakti, the divine female energy, so the word names a kind of Hindu devotee.

clue.text: Some rejected behind conductor in rickety bus?

definitions.note: the question mark marks a bus as just one example of a decrepit vehicle

indicators.note: behind means coming after, so this piece follows the conductor's name

parts.note: Sir Simon Rattle is a famous British orchestral conductor

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: some of something is a part of it

explanation.surface: Some passengers are turned away behind the conductor on a shaky old bus.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'conductor' looks like a bus conductor in the surface; it is the musician Simon Rattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A rattletrap is a rickety, worn-out vehicle that rattles as it goes, so a battered bus qualifies.

clue.text: Select underwear, they say for those eating out

indicators.note: they say signals what is heard in speech, so the sounds count rather than the spelling

parts.note: to pick is to select, and knickers are women's underpants

explanation.surface: Choosing lingerie, so people say, for diners outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Knickers is the British word for women's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Picnickers are people having a meal outdoors, which is eating out in its literal sense rather than at a restaurant.

clue.text: Wild cat outside not previously showing spirit

indicators.note: a word outside another surrounds it, so the cat's name wraps the inner piece

parts.note: the puma is a wild American cat
ne is an archaic word for not; previously marks it as old usage

explanation.surface: A wild cat, formerly unseen outdoors, shows some fighting spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneuma is the Greek word for breath, used in English for the soul or vital spirit.

clue.text: Kick about with woman, very old from the east

definitions.note: 'very old' marks the word as archaic

indicators.note: turned about means facing back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to toe a ball is to kick it with the toe
hen is informal for a woman, especially in Scotland

explanation.surface: An eastern old woman gets kicked around.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end with 'very old' telling you the word is obsolete.
explanation.definitionFit: Eothen is an archaic adverb meaning from the east, known from Kinglake's 1844 travel book of that title.

clue.text: Aged work in abridged edition?

parts.note: ae is a Chambers abbreviation for aged, from Latin aetatis

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
ed is the shortened form of edition

explanation.surface: An ancient piece of writing is offered in a cut-down printing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' reads as a noun for a book, but it is the instruction to rearrange IN and ED. The whole clue also describes the epic, an old work often read in abridged editions.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgil's Aeneid is a Latin epic poem over two thousand years old, so it is an aged literary work.

clue.text: Quiet and also term for mum

definitions.text: Quiet and also term for mum

parts.note: sh is the command for silence
too means and also, in addition

indicators.note: a term is an end or limit, so only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the last letter of mum

explanation.surface: Keep quiet, and that also goes for Mother.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the definition: the answer means quiet, and is another word for mum in its sense of silent. 'term' means end, so only the last letter of mum is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Shtoom (schtum) is Yiddish-derived slang for silent, as in 'keep shtoom', which is exactly what keeping mum means.

clue.text: Out of centre modern Afrikaner encampment

indicators.note: out of centre means the middle is missing, so the word loses its central letter

parts.note: later means more recent, more modern

explanation.surface: A new Afrikaner camp built away from the town centre.
explanation.walkthrough: LATER has five letters, so its centre is the third, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Laer is the Afrikaans form of laager, a defensive camp ringed by wagons, as made by Boer trekkers.

clue.text: Wavy Navy in Cornish resort first to leave

indicators.note: placed in something means put inside it
the first to leave is the opening letter, which departs from the word

parts.note: Bude is a seaside resort in north Cornwall; its first letter goes
N is the abbreviation for Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors flood into a Cornish seaside town and the first of them heads off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wavy Navy' was the nickname for the Royal Naval Volunteer Reserve, whose officers wore wavy sleeve braid; here the two words split.
explanation.definitionFit: Unde is a heraldic term for a line drawn in waves, so it means wavy.

clue.text: Brainy stuff coming regularly from Gallican

indicators.note: coming at regular intervals means taking every other letter, starting with the first

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Clever material keeps arriving from a French church source.
explanation.walkthrough: Gallican refers to the French Catholic church; it is only a source of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Glia are the supporting cells of the nervous system, found in the brain, so they are literally brain tissue.

clue.text: Reptile seen in Antigua naturally?

indicators.note: something seen in a phrase is visible inside it, running across the word boundary

parts.note: the letters run from the end of the island's name into the start of the adverb

explanation.surface: Where would you expect to spot this lizard? In Antigua, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: iguanas really do live on Antigua, so the clue reads as a statement of fact.
explanation.definitionFit: The iguana is a large tropical American lizard, and lizards are reptiles.

clue.text: Golfer's tip snubbed? Woods may gain holes from it

definitions.text: Woods may gain holes from it

indicators.note: snubbed here means docked or cut short, as a snub nose is short, so the word loses its end

parts.note: Ernie Els is a South African golfer
a tip is a piece of advice, a hint; its last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: A golfer's advice is ignored; perhaps Tiger Woods can pick up a few holes from it.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf picture makes 'Woods' Tiger Woods and 'holes' golf holes; really it is timber being bored.
explanation.definitionFit: An elshin is a Scots word for a shoemaker's awl, a pointed tool that pierces holes in wood or leather.

clue.text: Overheard saying in Greek department

indicators.note: something overheard is caught by ear, so it is the sound of the word that counts

parts.note: a gnome is a pithy saying or maxim

explanation.surface: A remark is eavesdropped in a Greek government office.
explanation.walkthrough: A gnome, besides a garden figure, is an aphorism; the silent G makes it sound the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A nome is one of the provinces into which modern Greece is divided, an administrative department.

clue.text: Taking sides, studies surprisingly passed over Northern Rock

indicators.note: taking away a word's sides means removing its outermost letters at each end
letters passed over something are laid across and around it, enclosing it
surprisingly means in an unexpected way, so the letters fall into an unexpected order

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters taken off
N is the abbreviation for Northern

explanation.surface: Picking sides, research unexpectedly ignored the failed bank Northern Rock.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Rock was a British bank that collapsed in 2007; the surface leans on it, but here Northern and Rock work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunite is an igneous rock made almost wholly of olivine, named after Dun Mountain in New Zealand.

clue.text: Film star Richard set about acting in outmoded clothing

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the surname surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: Richard Gere is an American film actor
A is an abbreviation for acting, as in a job title

explanation.surface: A Hollywood actor starts performing dressed in old-fashioned costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film star' and 'acting' seem to belong together, but acting only supplies one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Geare is an archaic spelling of gear, meaning dress or apparel, so it is clothing in an out-of-date form.

clue.text: Surrey town functions receiving cheers

indicators.note: receiving something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: sines are trigonometric functions
ta is British informal thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: Social events in a commuter town get a round of applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'functions' suggests parties, but these are maths functions. Staines is a town on the Thames near Heathrow; cheers and ta are both British ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Staines-upon-Thames is a town in Surrey, the county south-west of London, so it is a Surrey town by name.
